headline: Growth companies are paying for customers. Established brands are protecting margin.

lines.text: Sea's sales and marketing rose 64.5% to US$1.66bn in Q2 2026, faster than revenue (up 48%). Most of the increase came from Monee, its lending arm, where marketing more than doubled.
Grab grew sales and marketing 16% to US$107m in Q3, well behind revenue growth of 27%. Its bigger lever sits in incentives. Partner and consumer incentives each rose 26%, to US$737m combined.

VinFast's selling and distribution costs rose 69% in Q2 2026, to VND3.49 trillion (about US$139m at the company's own exchange rate). It says sales programmes and incentives on vehicles with deferred revenue were booked as selling expenses.

Established consumer brands cut back. QAF's A&P fell 18% to S$7.9m, which it puts down to "a rationalisation of marketing expenses by the Bakery segment". Haw Par cut 22%, Yeo Hiap Seng 16%, and F J Benjamin 42% in its latest half.

Food Empire went the other way, up 30% to US$30.2m on "more intense promotion and brand building activities". MoneyHero cut advertising and marketing 11.5% through what it calls "more disciplined, data-driven campaign allocation".

read: Growth companies are paying for customers while mature brands protect margin. If your client list leans toward the second group, your next pitch has to show what each dollar returns.
scope_watch: When an A&P budget drops by a fifth, the brief rarely shrinks with it. Watch for the same deliverables on a smaller fee, because that's where unbilled work quietly starts.
footnote: Periods differ by company because each reports on its own calendar. Every figure links to the filing it came from.
